what: A six-slide tour of Workbench that ships with the app: a short headline per slide, a real Workbench screenshot, one Draw-style annotation, and narration in manifest.json. It was designed and rendered from this folder; it was not made through Snap & Talk and does not show what a Snap & Talk handoff produces.
source: scripts/samples (deck.html, deck.css, backdrop.html, manifest.json, provenance.json, screens/, backdrops/)
renderer: Headless Google Chrome in two passes. Pass 1 draws the walls and soft window shadows from backdrop.html and saves them as backdrops/*.jpg (Chrome's PDF printer would otherwise turn them into large images). Pass 2 shoots each 1920x1080 CSS px slide of deck.html at device scale 2, reduced to 1600x900 JPEG (quality 82) with sips, and prints the same page as a six-page 1440x810 pt (16:9) PDF whose headlines, lines and notes are live text.

screenshots.origin: Workbench's own surface gallery, rendered offscreen from the app's SwiftUI pages with synthetic sample data. No real person's data, recordings or captures appear.

files.screens/dictate.png: sample-dictate-light.png from WORKBENCH_SAMPLE_SCREENS_GALLERY_ONLY=1 (Dictate with automatic paste set up)
files.screens/snap-and-talk.png: sample-snap-and-talk-light.png from WORKBENCH_SAMPLE_SCREENS_GALLERY_ONLY=1 (a four-screen walkthrough of real Workbench screens with narration)

screenshots.processing: Downscaled to 1600 px wide with sips -Z 1600. Pixels are otherwise unchanged, except that the Draw slide covers the offscreen render's "Ready on 0 displays" status line, which the installed app shows as "Ready on 1 display".

annotations: Drawn in SVG over the screenshots in Draw's default coral ink (#ff5446 on the website, InkColor.coral in the app); the cover ellipse is the website's hand-drawn mark in mint.
